introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
incertitudes: Question 2 (a) : l'équation imprimée contient le terme $y^2$, mais la formule à démontrer (coefficient 1.96 = 2 - 0.04 sur $y_n$) correspond à l'équation avec le terme $y$ (et non $y^2$). Le corrigé démontre la formule imprimée pour $y'' - xy' + y = 0$ et signale que, avec $y^2$ pris à la lettre, la formule serait différente ; la partie (ii) utilise la formule imprimée, comme le demande le sujet (résultat 1.7152 ; 1.6939 si l'on appliquait la version littérale avec $y^2$).

Question 2 (a)(i) : les parenthèses manquent dans la formule imprimée (« 1.96y_n - 1 + 0.1x_n y_{n-1} ») ; elle est lue comme (1.96y_n - (1 + 0.1x_n)y_{n-1}) / (1 - 0.1x_n), seule lecture compatible avec les approximations données. Le sujet écrit aussi « deferential » pour « differential ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $y$ satisfies the differential equation

$$
\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - x\frac{dy}{dx} + y^2 = 0,
$$

use the approximations

$$
h^2\left(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)_n \approx y_{n+1} - 2y_n + y_{n-1} \quad\text{and}\quad 2h\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)_n \approx y_{n+1} - y_{n-1},
$$

with a step length of $0.2$ to show that

$$
y_{n+1} = \frac{1.96\,y_n - (1 + 0.1x_n)\,y_{n-1}}{1 - 0.1x_n}.
$$

*[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Evaluate the equation at the point $x = x_n$ and replace each derivative by its central-difference approximation, with $h = 0.2$:

$$
\frac{y_{n+1} - 2y_n + y_{n-1}}{h^2} - x_n\,\frac{y_{n+1} - y_{n-1}}{2h} + (\text{last term}) = 0.
$$

Multiply by $h^2 = 0.04$. Since $\dfrac{h}{2} = 0.1$,

$$
y_{n+1} - 2y_n + y_{n-1} - 0.1x_n\,(y_{n+1} - y_{n-1}) + 0.04\,(\text{last term}) = 0.
$$

Collect the terms in $y_{n+1}$ on the left:

$$
(1 - 0.1x_n)\,y_{n+1} = 2y_n - 0.04\,(\text{last term}) - (1 + 0.1x_n)\,y_{n-1}.
$$

The formula to be shown has $1.96\,y_n = (2 - 0.04)\,y_n$, so the last term of the differential equation, evaluated at $x_n$, must be $y_n$ (the equation $y'' - xy' + y = 0$). Then

$$
(1 - 0.1x_n)\,y_{n+1} = 1.96\,y_n - (1 + 0.1x_n)\,y_{n-1},
\qquad\text{that is}\qquad
y_{n+1} = \frac{1.96\,y_n - (1 + 0.1x_n)\,y_{n-1}}{1 - 0.1x_n}.
$$

**Remark on the printed equation.** The statement prints the last term as $y^2$. Taken literally, the same steps give $(1 - 0.1x_n)\,y_{n+1} = 2y_n - 0.04\,y_n^2 - (1 + 0.1x_n)\,y_{n-1}$, which is not the expression to be shown; the coefficient $1.96$ of the printed result corresponds to the term $y$, so the exponent $2$ appears to be a misprint.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $y = 1$ when $x = 0$ and $y = 1.378$ when $x = 0.2$, find $y$ when $x = 0.4$, correct to $4$ decimal places. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the formula of part (i) with $n = 1$: $x_0 = 0$, $y_0 = 1$, $x_1 = 0.2$, $y_1 = 1.378$ and $x_2 = 0.4$.

$$
y_2 = \frac{1.96\,y_1 - (1 + 0.1x_1)\,y_0}{1 - 0.1x_1}
= \frac{1.96 \times 1.378 - (1 + 0.02)\times 1}{1 - 0.02}
= \frac{2.70088 - 1.02}{0.98}
= \frac{1.68088}{0.98}.
$$

$$
y_2 = 1.71518\ldots \approx 1.7152 \quad (4\ \text{d.p.}).
$$

So $y \approx 1.7152$ when $x = 0.4$.

(With the term $y^2$ read literally, the corresponding formula would give $1.6939$; the answer expected from the formula printed in (i) is $1.7152$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use Simpson's rule with three ordinates to estimate

$$
\int_0^1 e^{x^2}\,dx,
$$

giving your answer correct to $3$ decimal places. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three ordinates mean two strips of width $h = \dfrac{1 - 0}{2} = 0.5$, at $x = 0,\ 0.5,\ 1$. With $f(x) = e^{x^2}$:

| $x$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $1$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $e^{0.25} = 1.284025$ | $e = 2.718282$ |

Simpson's rule: $\displaystyle\int_a^b f\,dx \approx \frac{h}{3}\left[f_0 + 4f_1 + f_2\right]$.

$$
\int_0^1 e^{x^2}\,dx \approx \frac{0.5}{3}\left[1 + 4(1.284025) + 2.718282\right]
= \frac{1}{6}\,(8.854384) = 1.47573\ldots
$$

$$
\int_0^1 e^{x^2}\,dx \approx 1.476 \quad (3\ \text{d.p.}).
$$

(The exact value is $1.46265\ldots$; with only two strips the error is about $0.013$.)
